title: John R. P. French, Jr.: A Lewinian's Lewinian
display_name: John R. P. French, Jr.: A Lewinian's Lewinian

raw_affiliation_strings: JAMES S. HOUSE is Professor of Sociology and Director of the Survey Research Center in the Institute for Social Research at the University of Michigan. He began studying occupational stress and health in the late 1960s as a graduate student in social psychology at the university under the tutelage of John R. P. French, Jr. He has continued since then to study psychosocial factors in health, focusing during the late 1970s and 1980s on social relationships and supports as determinants of health and buffers against deleterious effects of stress, and currently on the role of social and psychological factors, especially socioeconomic status, in the maintenance of health and effective functioning in middle and later life

title: The Bases of Power: Origins and Recent Developments
display_name: The Bases of Power: Origins and Recent Developments

raw_affiliation_strings: BERTRAM H. RAVEN is Professor of Psychology at the University of California, Los Angeles. He received his Ph.D. in Social Psychology from the University of Michigan. While there, he was associated with the Research Center for Group Dynamics and worked closely with John R. P. French in the development of the Bases of Social Power model which is associated with their names. Though he has carried out research in various areas of social psychology (group performance; social comparison and self-evaluation; interdependence in group problem solving; cognitive dissonance and change in attitudes, beliefs, and behavior), it is theory and research in social power that has occupied his major attention. In addition to theoretical development, he has applied the basic theory to issues in health, education, and political behavior. Dr. Raven has been an active member of SPSSI; among other roles, he has served as both Editor of the Journal of Social Issues (1970–1973) and President of the Society (1973–1974). He is currently working on a book that will present in greater detail the Power/Interaction Model of Interpersonal Influence that is discussed in this article

VAN HARRISON is Director of the Office of Continuing Medical Education and Assistant Professor in the Department of Postgraduate Medicine and Health Professions Education at the University of Michigan, where he is also a Faculty Associate at the Institute for Social Research. raw_affiliation_strings: ANDRE MODIGLIANI received his Ph.D. in social psychology from the “old” joint program in sociology and psychology at the University of Michigan. He is an associate professor of sociology at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor. With William Gamson he has done two books: Untangling the Cold War: A Strategy for Testing Rival Theories and Conceptions of Social Life: A Text-Reader for Social Psychology. His recent work has dealt with media discourse on political issues and its relationship to public opinion. Currently, he is pursuing work on obedience and defiance to authority in both historical and laboratory contexts
